reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern consists of sharp, rectangular pulses (square-wave-like) with near-zero baseline, robust-standardized amplitude peaking at ~3.0 and returning abruptly to 0.0. Pulses are highly stable in height and shape across candidates, with negligible noise or curvature. The period is consistently ~97 points per cycle (as confirmed by catalog window_cycles: 1P=97, 3P=291≈3×97, 5P=485≈5×97), and inter-pulse intervals are uniform within each candidate. Each pulse rises and falls nearly vertically (slope magnitude large, duration ≤2–3 points), indicating step-like transitions. Baseline is flat at 0.0 with no trend in candidates 0, 2, and 3; candidate 1 shows a barely detectable positive slope (~0.0103 per point) over its 291-point span, but pulse morphology remains identical. No troughs below baseline occur; all minima are exactly 0.0. Amplitude_90 is uniformly 2.995 across all references, confirming tight amplitude control. Acceptable variation includes minor timing jitter (<±1 point) in pulse onset and negligible baseline drift only when spanning >1 cycle—otherwise, the pattern is rigidly periodic and deterministic. No smoothing, ringing, or partial pulses appear; truncation at boundaries is clean (full pulses visible, no half-pulses).

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 0 for single-pulse queries (e.g., short windows or isolated events); use reference 2 as primary template for multi-cycle analysis due to its perfect baseline stability and morphological fidelity; reference 3 is optimal for long-window validation or when assessing periodic consistency over ≥5 cycles; reference 1 may be used cautiously when a slight monotonic drift is observed in query—but only if pulse morphology matches exactly, as drift alone does not indicate anomaly.
